previous_assumption: assumed indicativeRateUnit on a QuotationResponse could be freely chosen by whoever is responding, and that Requirement.quantity being just a bare integer with no downstream wiring was fine since nothing was reported broken
correction: Client asked whether free unit choice while responding was a good approach -- checked and it was an actual live bug, not just a smell: the requirement detail page's lowest-rate and rate-spread comparison compared indicativeRate as a raw number across responses with zero unit normalization (6000/day vs 150000/month compared as 6000 vs 150000). Client chose to lock the response's unit to the requirement's own expectedDurationUnit (when set) rather than normalize the math -- enforced server-side in QuotationResponseService.submitResponse regardless of what the caller submits, frontend just avoids showing a picker whose value would be silently overridden. Comparison page still guards the residual case (requirement has no expectedDurationUnit, so responses can still land in different units) by refusing to compute lowest/spread across a mixed-unit set. Separately, client asked about a Requirement asking for quantity 3 when a responding Rental Company only has 1 matching machine -- confirmed Requirement.quantity is not wired to Rental or CommercialQuotation at all (both are single-machine records), so there is no defined fulfillment model for quantity greater than 1 today. Client chose the lightweight fix only: show the responding company their own machine count for that subcategory next to the response form when it is short of the required quantity, informational only, no submission block, no fulfillment-tracking redesign.
